dedupe_keys.name: gnss raw measurement and interference datasets from the 40th and 41st laura bassi expeditions to antarctica 2024 to 2026

description: Two datasets published by Aljaž Blatnik and Franc Dimc of the University of Ljubljana hold raw GNSS receiver measurements recorded continuously on the Italian research icebreaker Laura Bassi, operated by OGS, during Italian expeditions to Antarctica. The 40th expedition set covers 200 days from 7 October 2024 to 24 April 2025 with multi-constellation L1 observations. The 41st expedition set, with Blaz Bertalanic of the Jožef Stefan Institute, covers 216 days from 26 September 2025 to 29 April 2026 on a closed loop from Trieste to the Ross Sea and back through the Panama Canal and round Cape Horn, crossing the Antarctic Circle eight times, with L1 and L5 observations and RINEX 3.04 files. Daily u-blox UBX files include position and time, satellite metadata, raw pseudorange and carrier phase, RF front-end diagnostics with jamming indicators and 256-bin spectra, which let users see interference events along the voyage; a companion GitHub release gives access and visualisation code. Coverage: ship tracks spanning about 120 degrees of latitude. Format and access: ZIP archives of about 45.7 GB and 80.3 GB on Zenodo, free of charge under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0. Caveats: one consumer-grade receiver on a moving ship; interference sources are not identified; the size needs planning before download. Simulation uses: hazard exposure and resilience of GNSS-dependent navigation and timing to interference and ionospheric effects at high latitude, and validation of interference detection. Related records: GPSJam maps aircraft-reported interference, IGS products give reference orbits and clocks, and Kshana can simulate jamming resilience.
